story: On a sunny Friday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary stands on Magnolia Loop with a paddle in hand, sheepish but upbeat, after admitting he lost track of the wiring on his golf cart. Donna, flustered but determined, is thinning out the pink flamingo flock in her yard so that only three remain visible from the street, while Hal reminds Gary that the review committee has to approve the new lights before they go on the cart. Meanwhile, eager Rosa is at home checking her shift schedule to make sure nothing cuts into tonight's dinner.
events: Donna (donna flamingo flock): Pull the extra flamingos out of the yard until only three are left visible from the street
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Check that no per-diem shift cuts into tonight's dinner

gary.thought_process: I already asked Hal about my cart request last tick and he didn't answer me, he was busy with Donna's flamingo count. Asking again would just be nagging. Donna's waiting on me for the courts and I promised ten sharp, and it's past noon. The wiring is done and the lights are bagged, so the cart can wait until Hal's ruling comes through. Best thing is to own up to being late, grab my paddle, and walk with Donna to the rec center, keeping the partnership going.

parameters.content: You're right, Donna, I got tangled up in wiring and lost track. Paddle's in hand. Lead the way and I'll buy the lemonades after.

donna.thought_process: Hal says my flamingo flock is over the L-02 limit of three, and he's got the count written down. I can pull a few flamingos out of the yard right now and keep the log in his pocket, which is easy and free. Then I can drag Gary to the courts. Gary's busy with Hal about his cart request, so fix the flamingos first and let them finish their business.

parameters.content: Pull the extra flamingos out of the yard until only three are left visible from the street

hal.thought_process: Gary asked whether his request is on my desk, and he's earned a straight answer. I'm not the committee, so I can only be honest about what I know. Donna is dragging him off to pickleball anyway, so keep it short and factual. Rules say exterior cart mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, and I'd rather he get it right than get reported. I'll tell him to confirm it's filed with the committee and that I'll note his wiring is done. Keep my temper out of it and let the record speak.

parameters.content: Gary, I'm not the one who approves it, the review committee is. Make sure it's actually filed with them before those lights go on the cart, because L-01 doesn't care how neat the wiring is.

rosa.thought_process: It's 1:17 PM Friday and I've already set the places and left room for Gary's extra chairs. The main dish is on and the sides are staged. I keep circling the same prep, and I've checked the schedule plenty. Time to look at the shift schedule one last time to make sure nothing conflicts with tonight, since I'm still picking up per-diem shifts, then I can stop fussing and let the food rest until guests arrive.

parameters.content: Check that no per-diem shift cuts into tonight's dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
